verses.english: Then all the people of the surrounding country of the Gerasenes asked him to leave them, for they were seized with great fear. So he got into the boat and returned.
verses.greek: καὶ ἠρώτησεν αὐτὸν ἅπαν τὸ πλῆθος τῆς περιχώρου τῶν Γερασηνῶν ἀπελθεῖν ἀπ’ αὐτῶν, ὅτι φόβῳ μεγάλῳ συνείχοντο· αὐτὸς δὲ ἐμβὰς εἰς πλοῖον ὑπέστρεψεν.

verses.english: The man from whom the daimons had gone out begged that he might be with him; but he sent him away, saying,
verses.greek: ἐδεῖτο δὲ αὐτοῦ ὁ ἀνὴρ ἀφ’ οὗ ἐξεληλύθει τὰ δαιμόνια εἶναι σὺν αὐτῷ· ἀπέλυσεν δὲ αὐτὸν λέγων·

verses.english: "Return to your home, and tell how much God has done for you." And he went away, proclaiming throughout the whole town how much Jesus had done for him.
verses.greek: Ὑπόστρεφε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου, καὶ διηγοῦ ὅσα σοι ἐποίησεν ὁ θεός. καὶ ἀπῆλθεν καθ’ ὅλην τὴν πόλιν κηρύσσων ὅσα ἐποίησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς.

verses.english: When Jesus returned, the crowd welcomed him, for they were all waiting for him.
verses.greek: Ἐν δὲ τῷ ὑποστρέφειν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπεδέξατο αὐτὸν ὁ ὄχλος, ἦσαν γὰρ πάντες προσδοκῶντες αὐτόν.

verses.english: Then a man named Jairus came, a leader of the synagogue. He fell at Jesus' feet and begged him to come to his house,
verses.greek: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἦλθεν ἀνὴρ ᾧ ὄνομα Ἰάϊρος, καὶ οὗτος ἄρχων τῆς συναγωγῆς ὑπῆρχεν, καὶ πεσὼν παρὰ τοὺς πόδας τοῦ Ἰησοῦ παρεκάλει αὐτὸν εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ,

verses.english: for he had an only daughter, about twelve years old, and she was dying. As he went, the crowds pressed in on him.
verses.greek: ὅτι θυγάτηρ μονογενὴς ἦν αὐτῷ ὡς ἐτῶν δώδεκα καὶ αὐτὴ ἀπέθνῃσκεν. Ἐν δὲ τῷ ὑπάγειν αὐτὸν οἱ ὄχλοι συνέπνιγον αὐτόν.

verses.english: And a woman who had suffered from a flow of blood for twelve years, and had spent all she had on physicians, and could not be healed by anyone,
verses.greek: καὶ γυνὴ οὖσα ἐν ῥύσει αἵματος ἀπὸ ἐτῶν δώδεκα, ἥτις ἰατροῖς προσαναλώσασα ὅλον τὸν βίον οὐκ ἴσχυσεν ἀπ’ οὐδενὸς θεραπευθῆναι,

verses.english: came up behind him and touched the fringe of his cloak, and immediately her flow of blood stopped.
verses.greek: προσελθοῦσα ὄπισθεν ἥψατο τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ, καὶ παραχρῆμα ἔστη ἡ ῥύσις τοῦ αἵματος αὐτῆς.

verses.english: Jesus said, "Who touched me?" When all denied it, Peter said, "Master, the crowds are surrounding you and pressing in on you."
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Τίς μου ἥψατο; ἀρνουμένων δὲ πάντων εἶπεν ὁ Πέτρος· Ἐπιστάτα, οἱ ὄχλοι συνέχουσίν σε καὶ ἀποθλίβουσιν.

verses.english: But Jesus said, "Someone touched me; for I know that power has gone out from me."
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ἥψατό μού τις, ἐγὼ γὰρ ἔγνων δύναμιν ἐξεληλυθυῖαν ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ.

verses.english: When the woman saw that she could not remain hidden, she came trembling, and falling down before him she declared in the presence of all the people why she had touched him and how she had been healed at once.
verses.greek: ἰδοῦσα δὲ ἡ γυνὴ ὅτι οὐκ ἔλαθεν τρέμουσα ἦλθεν καὶ προσπεσοῦσα αὐτῷ δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν ἥψατο αὐτοῦ ἀπήγγειλεν ἐνώπιον παντὸς τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ ὡς ἰάθη παραχρῆμα.

verses.english: He said to her, "Daughter, your faith has saved you; go in peace."
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Θυγάτηρ, ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε· πορεύου εἰς εἰρήνην.

verses.english: While he was still speaking, someone came from the house of the leader of the synagogue and said, "Your daughter is dead; do not trouble the teacher any longer."
verses.greek: Ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἔρχεταί τις παρὰ τοῦ ἀρχισυναγώγου λέγων ὅτι Τέθνηκεν ἡ θυγάτηρ σου, μηκέτι σκύλλε τὸν διδάσκαλον.

verses.english: When Jesus heard this, he answered him, "Do not be afraid; only believe, and she will be saved."
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἀκούσας ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ· Μὴ φοβοῦ, μόνον πίστευσον, καὶ σωθήσεται.

verses.english: When he came to the house, he let no one go in with him except Peter, John and James, and the child's father and mother.
verses.greek: ἐλθὼν δὲ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν οὐκ ἀφῆκεν εἰσελθεῖν τινα σὺν αὐτῷ εἰ μὴ Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ τὸν πατέρα τῆς παιδὸς καὶ τὴν μητέρα.

verses.english: Everyone was weeping and mourning for her; but he said, "Do not weep, for she is not dead but asleep."
verses.greek: ἔκλαιον δὲ πάντες καὶ ἐκόπτοντο αὐτήν. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Μὴ κλαίετε, οὐ γὰρ ἀπέθανεν ἀλλὰ καθεύδει.

verses.english: And they laughed at him, knowing that she was dead.
verses.greek: καὶ κατεγέλων αὐτοῦ, εἰδότες ὅτι ἀπέθανεν.

verses.english: But he took her by the hand and called out, "Child, get up!"
verses.greek: αὐτὸς δὲ κρατήσας τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῆς ἐφώνησεν λέγων· Ἡ παῖς, ἔγειρε.

verses.english: Her spirit returned, and she got up at once; and he directed that she be given something to eat.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐπέστρεψεν τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτῆς, καὶ ἀνέστη παραχρῆμα, καὶ διέταξεν αὐτῇ δοθῆναι φαγεῖν.

verses.english: Her parents were amazed; but he ordered them to tell no one what had happened.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐξέστησαν οἱ γονεῖς αὐτῆς· ὁ δὲ παρήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς μηδενὶ εἰπεῖν τὸ γεγονός.

verses.english: He called the twelve together and gave them power and authority over all daimons and to cure diseases,
verses.greek: Συγκαλεσάμενος δὲ τοὺς δώδεκα ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς δύναμιν καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἐπὶ πάντα τὰ δαιμόνια καὶ νόσους θεραπεύειν,

verses.english: and he sent them out to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal.
verses.greek: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς κηρύσσειν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἰᾶσθαι,

verses.english: He said to them, "Take nothing for the journey: no staff, no bag, no bread, no money, and do not have two tunics.
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Μηδὲν αἴρετε εἰς τὴν ὁδόν, μήτε ῥάβδον μήτε πήραν μήτε ἄρτον μήτε ἀργύριον, μήτε ἀνὰ δύο χιτῶνας ἔχειν.

verses.english: Whatever house you enter, stay there, and leave from there.
verses.greek: καὶ εἰς ἣν ἂν οἰκίαν εἰσέλθητε, ἐκεῖ μένετε καὶ ἐκεῖθεν ἐξέρχεσθε.

verses.english: Wherever they do not welcome you, as you leave that town shake the dust off your feet as a testimony against them."
verses.greek: καὶ ὅσοι ἂν μὴ δέχωνται ὑμᾶς, ἐξερχόμενοι ἀπὸ τῆς πόλεως ἐκείνης τὸν κονιορτὸν ἀπὸ τῶν ποδῶν ὑμῶν ἀποτινάσσετε εἰς μαρτύριον ἐπ’ αὐτούς.

verses.english: They set out and went through the villages, bringing the good news and curing people everywhere.
verses.greek: ἐξερχόμενοι δὲ διήρχοντο κατὰ τὰς κώμας εὐαγγελιζόμενοι καὶ θεραπεύοντες πανταχοῦ.

verses.english: Herod the tetrarch heard about all that was happening, and he was perplexed, because it was said by some that John had been raised from the dead,
verses.greek: Ἤκουσεν δὲ Ἡρῴδης ὁ τετραάρχης τὰ γινόμενα πάντα, καὶ διηπόρει διὰ τὸ λέγεσθαι ὑπό τινων ὅτι Ἰωάννης ἠγέρθη ἐκ νεκρῶν,

verses.english: by some that Elijah had appeared, and by others that one of the ancient prophets had arisen.
verses.greek: ὑπό τινων δὲ ὅτι Ἠλίας ἐφάνη, ἄλλων δὲ ὅτι προφήτης τις τῶν ἀρχαίων ἀνέστη.

verses.english: Herod said, "John I beheaded; but who is this about whom I hear such things?" And he tried to see him.
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Ἡρῴδης· Ἰωάννην ἐγὼ ἀπεκεφάλισα· τίς δέ ἐστιν οὗτος περὶ οὗ ἀκούω τοιαῦτα; καὶ ἐζήτει ἰδεῖν αὐτόν.

verses.english: When the emissaries returned, they told him all that they had done. He took them with him and withdrew privately to a town called Bethsaida.
verses.greek: Καὶ ὑποστρέψαντες οἱ ἀπόστολοι διηγήσαντο αὐτῷ ὅσα ἐποίησαν. καὶ παραλαβὼν αὐτοὺς ὑπεχώρησεν κατ’ ἰδίαν εἰς πόλιν καλουμένην Βηθσαϊδά.

verses.english: When the crowds found out, they followed him; and he welcomed them, spoke to them about the kingdom of God, and healed those who needed healing.
verses.greek: οἱ δὲ ὄχλοι γνόντες ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ. καὶ ἀποδεξάμενος αὐτοὺς ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς περὶ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ τοὺς χρείαν ἔχοντας θεραπείας ἰᾶτο.

verses.english: The day began to decline, and the twelve came to him and said, "Send the crowd away, so that they may go into the surrounding villages and countryside to find lodging and provisions; for we are here in a deserted place."
verses.greek: Ἡ δὲ ἡμέρα ἤρξατο κλίνειν· προσελθόντες δὲ οἱ δώδεκα εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ἀπόλυσον τὸν ὄχλον, ἵνα πορευθέντες εἰς τὰς κύκλῳ κώμας καὶ ἀγροὺς καταλύσωσιν καὶ εὕρωσιν ἐπισιτισμόν, ὅτι ὧδε ἐν ἐρήμῳ τόπῳ ἐσμέν.

verses.english: But he said to them, "You give them something to eat." They said, "We have no more than five loaves and two fish, unless we are to go and buy food for all these people."
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Δότε αὐτοῖς ὑμεῖς φαγεῖν. οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Οὐκ εἰσὶν ἡμῖν πλεῖον ἢ ἄρτοι πέντε καὶ ἰχθύες δύο, εἰ μήτι πορευθέντες ἡμεῖς ἀγοράσωμεν εἰς πάντα τὸν λαὸν τοῦτον βρώματα.

verses.english: For there were about five thousand men. And he said to his disciples, "Make them sit down in groups of about fifty each."
verses.greek: ἦσαν γὰρ ὡσεὶ ἄνδρες πεντακισχίλιοι. εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ· Κατακλίνατε αὐτοὺς κλισίας ὡσεὶ ἀνὰ πεντήκοντα.

verses.english: They did so, and made them all sit down.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐποίησαν οὕτως καὶ κατέκλιναν ἅπαντας.

verses.english: And taking the five loaves and the two fish, he looked up to heaven and blessed over them, and broke them, and gave them to the disciples to set before the crowd.
verses.greek: λαβὼν δὲ τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εὐλόγησεν ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς καὶ κατέκλασεν καὶ ἐδίδου τοῖς μαθηταῖς παραθεῖναι τῷ ὄχλῳ.

verses.english: And all ate and were filled; and what was left over was gathered up, twelve baskets of broken pieces.
verses.greek: καὶ ἔφαγον καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν πάντες, καὶ ἤρθη τὸ περισσεῦσαν αὐτοῖς κλασμάτων κόφινοι δώδεκα.

notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.20.4–7: "a multitude of daimons in one man", the name "legion", the cry that Jesus is "son of God", and the plea not to be sent into the abyss, which he says Jesus granted ("Denique impetraverunt"). The binding with chains (8:29), the drowning of the herd and the reaction of the townspeople (8:33–39) are not cited and are printed in grey.

Reception. Tertullian argues that the daimons knew whose son Jesus was because they feared the Creator's abyss, and that Jesus' granting their request proves he belonged to that God (Marc. 4.20.5–7). The text itself says only that they begged not to be sent into the abyss (ἄβυσσος, the deep in the Greek Bible).

notes.term: The woman who touched his cloak (8:42b–48)
notes.explanation: Epiphanius, sch. 14: »ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ ὑπάγειν αὐτούς, συνέπνιγον αὐτὸν οἱ ὄχλοι. καὶ γυνὴ ἁψαμένη αὐτοῦ ἰάθη τοῦ αἵματος· καὶ εἶπεν ὁ κύριος· τίς μου ἥψατο;« and »ἥψατό μού τις. καὶ γὰρ ἔγνων δύναμιν ἐξελθοῦσαν ἀπ' ἐμοῦ«. Tertullian, Marc. 4.20.7–13: "Quis me, inquit, tetigit?… Tetigit me aliquis… Sensi enim virtutem ex me profectam… Fides tua te salvam fecit." Both witnesses give the question as "Who touched me?" (τίς μου ἥψατο;) where NA27 has "Who is the one who touched me?"; the attested form is printed. 8:47 is not cited and is printed in grey.

notes.term: The woman and the law of purity
notes.explanation: Reception and interpretation. The Marcionites read the healing as Jesus setting aside the law that made a woman with a flow of blood unclean (Lev 15:25–27). Tertullian answers that the law concerns the regular flow, not a disease, and that the woman did not break it (Marc. 4.20.9–12). The text itself says nothing about the law: it reports the touch, the power going out, and the woman's faith. The legal questions belong to the readers.

No witness cites the request of Jairus or the raising of his daughter. Epiphanius' quotation begins "as they were going", which presupposes the journey to Jairus' house, and NA27 prints 8:40–56 as one paragraph. The frame is therefore printed in grey, as part of an attested passage. Tertullian had already used the raising of the widow's son (7:11–17) to argue that raising the dead was the Creator's sign (4.18.2), so a second raising would add nothing to his case. That is why his silence here is not counted as evidence of absence.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.21.1: the disciples are sent to preach the kingdom of God, are forbidden to take food or clothing for the road, and are told to shake the dust from their feet "as a testimony". 9:1–2 and 9:6 are also read in the Dialogue of Adamantius (82,2–7) by the orthodox speaker, as an argument the Marcionite is expected to accept; Roth counts this as attestation. 9:4 is not cited and is printed in grey.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.21.2: "some said John, some Elijah, some one of the ancient prophets". He argues that whichever of these Jesus was, he was not raised to preach another god. 9:9 is not cited and is printed in grey.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.21.2–5 compares the feeding with the manna and with Elisha's loaves (2 Kgs 4:42–44); Epiphanius, sch. 15 quotes 9:16 as »ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εὐλόγησεν ἐπ' αὐτούς« ("he blessed over them"), printed here (Roth: very likely). 9:10–11 and 9:15 are not cited and are printed in grey. The previous text treated the distribution clause of 9:16 as an excision; no witness supports that.

Both this text and canonical Luke pass from the feeding (Mark 6:30–44) to Peter's confession (Mark 8:27–30) and lack the intervening block of Mark (6:45–8:26). The previous note presented this "Great Omission" as evidence that Proto-Luke is independent of Mark; since canonical Luke lacks the same block, it tells nothing about the relation between the two texts (audit context §5).

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 7
chapters.preamble: Peter's confession and what follows from it. Asked who he is, Peter answers "the Christ of God", and Jesus at once speaks of suffering, rejection, death and being raised "after three days" (the form of Mark and of both witnesses). On the mountain he is seen with Moses and Elijah, and the voice from the cloud says "This is my beloved son; listen to him." Tertullian dwells on this scene to argue that Jesus stands with the law and the prophets, not against them (Marc. 4.22). Then come the epileptic boy ("O faithless generation", without "and perverse"), the dispute about greatness, the Samaritan village where Jesus rebukes the disciples' wish to call down fire, and three would-be followers. Unattested verses inside these passages are printed in grey. The strange exorcist (9:49–50), which no witness cites, is not printed.

verses.english: Once, when he was praying alone, with only the disciples near him, he asked them, "Who do the crowds say that I am?"
verses.greek: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτὸν προσευχόμενον κατὰ μόνας συνῆσαν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταί, καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτοὺς λέγων· Τίνα με λέγουσιν οἱ ὄχλοι εἶναι;

verses.english: They answered, "John the Baptist; others, Elijah; and others, that one of the ancient prophets has arisen."
verses.greek: οἱ δὲ ἀποκριθέντες εἶπαν· Ἰωάννην τὸν βαπτιστήν, ἄλλοι δὲ Ἠλίαν, ἄλλοι δὲ ὅτι προφήτης τις τῶν ἀρχαίων ἀνέστη.

verses.english: He said to them, "But who do you say that I am?" Peter answered, "The Christ of God."
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ὑμεῖς δὲ τίνα με λέγετε εἶναι; Πέτρος δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Τὸν χριστὸν τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.english: He sternly ordered them to tell this to no one,
verses.greek: Ὁ δὲ ἐπιτιμήσας αὐτοῖς παρήγγειλεν μηδενὶ λέγειν τοῦτο,

verses.english: saying, "The son of man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and after three days be raised."
verses.greek: εἰπὼν ὅτι Δεῖ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου πολλὰ παθεῖν καὶ ἀποδοκιμασθῆναι ἀπὸ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ ἀρχιερέων καὶ γραμματέων καὶ ἀποκτανθῆναι καὶ μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἐγερθῆναι.

verses.english: Then he said to all, "If anyone wants to come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me.
verses.greek: Ἔλεγεν δὲ πρὸς πάντας· Εἴ τις θέλει ὀπίσω μου ἔρχεσθαι, ἀρνησάσθω ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀράτω τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ καθ’ ἡμέραν, καὶ ἀκολουθείτω μοι.

verses.english: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for my sake will save it.
verses.greek: ὃς γὰρ ἂν θέλῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ σῶσαι, ἀπολέσει αὐτήν· ὃς δ’ ἂν ἀπολέσῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ, οὗτος σώσει αὐτήν.

verses.english: What does it profit a man to gain the whole world, and lose or forfeit himself?
verses.greek: τί γὰρ ὠφελεῖται ἄνθρωπος κερδήσας τὸν κόσμον ὅλον ἑαυτὸν δὲ ἀπολέσας ἢ ζημιωθείς;

verses.english: For whoever is ashamed of me and of my words, of him the son of man will be ashamed when he comes in his glory and the glory of the Father and of the holy angels.
verses.greek: ὃς γὰρ ἂν ἐπαισχυνθῇ με καὶ τοὺς ἐμοὺς λόγους, τοῦτον ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπαισχυνθήσεται, ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἐν τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ καὶ τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τῶν ἁγίων ἀγγέλων.

verses.english: But truly I tell you, there are some standing here who will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God."
verses.greek: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ἀληθῶς, εἰσίν τινες τῶν αὐτοῦ ἑστηκότων οἳ οὐ μὴ γεύσωνται θανάτου ἕως ἂν ἴδωσιν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.english: About eight days after these sayings he took Peter and John and James and went up the mountain to pray.
verses.greek: Ἐγένετο δὲ μετὰ τοὺς λόγους τούτους ὡσεὶ ἡμέραι ὀκτὼ καὶ παραλαβὼν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην καὶ Ἰάκωβον ἀνέβη εἰς τὸ ὄρος προσεύξασθαι.

verses.english: And while he was praying, the appearance of his face changed, and his clothing became dazzling white.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ προσεύχεσθαι αὐτὸν τὸ εἶδος τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ ἕτερον καὶ ὁ ἱματισμὸς αὐτοῦ λευκὸς ἐξαστράπτων.

verses.english: And behold, two men were talking with him, Moses and Elijah,
verses.greek: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες δύο συνελάλουν αὐτῷ, οἵτινες ἦσαν Μωϋσῆς καὶ Ἠλίας,

verses.english: who appeared in glory.
verses.greek: οἳ ὀφθέντες ἐν δόξῃ.

verses.english: Peter and those with him were heavy with sleep; but when they were fully awake, they saw his glory and the two men standing with him.
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος καὶ οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ ἦσαν βεβαρημένοι ὕπνῳ· διαγρηγορήσαντες δὲ εἶδον τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ καὶ τοὺς δύο ἄνδρας τοὺς συνεστῶτας αὐτῷ.

verses.english: As they were leaving him, Peter said to Jesus, "Master, it is good for us to be here; let us make three tents, one for you, one for Moses and one for Elijah", not knowing what he was saying.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ διαχωρίζεσθαι αὐτοὺς ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ εἶπεν ὁ Πέτρος πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν· Ἐπιστάτα, καλόν ἐστιν ἡμᾶς ὧδε εἶναι, καὶ ποιήσωμεν σκηνὰς τρεῖς, μίαν σοὶ καὶ μίαν Μωϋσεῖ καὶ μίαν Ἠλίᾳ, μὴ εἰδὼς ὃ λέγει.

verses.english: While he was saying this, a cloud came and overshadowed them; and they were afraid as they entered the cloud.
verses.greek: ταῦτα δὲ αὐτοῦ λέγοντος ἐγένετο νεφέλη καὶ ἐπεσκίαζεν αὐτούς· ἐφοβήθησαν δὲ ἐν τῷ εἰσελθεῖν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν νεφέλην.

verses.english: And a voice came out of the cloud, saying, "This is my beloved son; listen to him."
verses.greek: καὶ φωνὴ ἐγένετο ἐκ τῆς νεφέλης λέγουσα· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, αὐτοῦ ἀκούετε.

verses.english: When the voice had spoken, Jesus was found alone. And they kept silent and in those days told no one any of the things they had seen.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐν τῷ γενέσθαι τὴν φωνὴν εὑρέθη Ἰησοῦς μόνος. καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐσίγησαν καὶ οὐδενὶ ἀπήγγειλαν ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις οὐδὲν ὧν ἑώρακαν.

verses.english: On the next day, when they had come down from the mountain, a great crowd met him.
verses.greek: Ἐγένετο δὲ τῇ ἑξῆς ἡμέρᾳ κατελθόντων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄρους συνήντησεν αὐτῷ ὄχλος πολύς.

verses.english: And a man from the crowd cried out, "Teacher, I beg you to look at my son, for he is my only child.
verses.greek: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου ἐβόησεν λέγων· Διδάσκαλε, δέομαί σου ἐπιβλέψαι ἐπὶ τὸν υἱόν μου, ὅτι μονογενής μοί ἐστιν,

verses.english: A spirit seizes him, and suddenly he cries out; it convulses him until he foams, and it hardly leaves him, battering him.
verses.greek: καὶ ἰδοὺ πνεῦμα λαμβάνει αὐτόν, καὶ ἐξαίφνης κράζει, καὶ σπαράσσει αὐτὸν μετὰ ἀφροῦ καὶ μόγις ἀποχωρεῖ ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ συντρῖβον αὐτόν·

verses.english: I begged your disciples to cast it out, but they could not."
verses.greek: καὶ ἐδεήθην τῶν μαθητῶν σου ἵνα ἐκβάλωσιν αὐτό, καὶ οὐκ ἠδυνήθησαν.

verses.english: Jesus answered, "O faithless generation, how long shall I be with you and bear with you? Bring your son here."
verses.greek: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ὦ γενεὰ ἄπιστος, ἕως πότε ἔσομαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς καὶ ἀνέξομαι ὑμῶν; προσάγαγε ὧδε τὸν υἱόν σου.

verses.english: While he was coming, the daimon threw him down and convulsed him. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.
verses.greek: ἔτι δὲ προσερχομένου αὐτοῦ ἔρρηξεν αὐτὸν τὸ δαιμόνιον καὶ συνεσπάραξεν· ἐπετίμησεν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἀκαθάρτῳ, καὶ ἰάσατο τὸν παῖδα καὶ ἀπέδωκεν αὐτὸν τῷ πατρὶ αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: And all were astounded at the greatness of God. While everyone was marvelling at all that he was doing, he said to his disciples,
verses.greek: ἐξεπλήσσοντο δὲ πάντες ἐπὶ τῇ μεγαλειότητι τοῦ θεοῦ. Πάντων δὲ θαυμαζόντων ἐπὶ πᾶσιν οἷς ἐποίει εἶπεν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ·

verses.english: "Let these words sink into your ears: the son of man is about to be handed over into human hands."
verses.greek: Θέσθε ὑμεῖς εἰς τὰ ὦτα ὑμῶν τοὺς λόγους τούτους, ὁ γὰρ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου μέλλει παραδίδοσθαι εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων.

verses.english: But they did not understand this saying; it was concealed from them, so that they could not perceive it, and they were afraid to ask him about it.
verses.greek: οἱ δὲ ἠγνόουν τὸ ῥῆμα τοῦτο, καὶ ἦν παρακεκαλυμμένον ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ἵνα μὴ αἴσθωνται αὐτό, καὶ ἐφοβοῦντο ἐρωτῆσαι αὐτὸν περὶ τοῦ ῥήματος τούτου.

verses.english: An argument arose among them as to which of them was the greatest.
verses.greek: Εἰσῆλθεν δὲ διαλογισμὸς ἐν αὐτοῖς, τὸ τίς ἂν εἴη μείζων αὐτῶν.

verses.english: But Jesus, knowing the thoughts of their hearts, took a little child and set it beside him,
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἰδὼς τὸν διαλογισμὸν τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν ἐπιλαβόμενος παιδίον ἔστησεν αὐτὸ παρ’ ἑαυτῷ,

verses.english: and said to them, "Whoever welcomes this child in my name welcomes me, and whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me; for the least among all of you is the greatest."
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὃς ἐὰν δέξηται τοῦτο τὸ παιδίον ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου ἐμὲ δέχεται, καὶ ὃς ἂν ἐμὲ δέξηται δέχεται τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με· ὁ γὰρ μικρότερος ἐν πᾶσιν ὑμῖν ὑπάρχων οὗτός ἐστιν μέγας.

verses.english: When the days were drawing near for him to be taken up, he set his face to go to Jerusalem,
verses.greek: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ συμπληροῦσθαι τὰς ἡμέρας τῆς ἀναλήμψεως αὐτοῦ καὶ αὐτὸς τὸ πρόσωπον ἐστήρισεν τοῦ πορεύεσθαι εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ,

verses.english: and he sent messengers ahead of him. They went and entered a village of the Samaritans to make ready for him;
verses.greek: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν ἀγγέλους πρὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ. καὶ πορευθέντες εἰσῆλθον εἰς κώμην Σαμαριτῶν, ὡς ἑτοιμάσαι αὐτῷ·

verses.english: but they did not receive him, because his face was set towards Jerusalem.
verses.greek: καὶ οὐκ ἐδέξαντο αὐτόν, ὅτι τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ἦν πορευόμενον εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ.

verses.english: When the disciples James and John saw it, they said, "Lord, do you want us to command fire to come down from heaven and consume them?"
verses.greek: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωάννης εἶπαν· Κύριε, θέλεις εἴπωμεν πῦρ καταβῆναι ἀπὸ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ἀναλῶσαι αὐτούς;

verses.english: But he turned and rebuked them.
verses.greek: στραφεὶς δὲ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτοῖς.

verses.english: And they went on to another village.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐπορεύθησαν εἰς ἑτέραν κώμην.

verses.english: As they were going along the road, someone said to him, "I will follow you wherever you go."
verses.greek: Καὶ πορευομένων αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ εἶπέν τις πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἀκολουθήσω σοι ὅπου ἐὰν ἀπέρχῃ.

verses.english: Jesus said to him, "Foxes have holes, and the birds of the sky have nests, but the son of man has nowhere to lay his head."
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Αἱ ἀλώπεκες φωλεοὺς ἔχουσιν καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατασκηνώσεις, ὁ δὲ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἔχει ποῦ τὴν κεφαλὴν κλίνῃ.

verses.english: To another he said, "Follow me." But he said, "Lord, first let me go and bury my father."
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς ἕτερον· Ἀκολούθει μοι. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Κύριε, ἐπίτρεψόν μοι ἀπελθόντι πρῶτον θάψαι τὸν πατέρα μου.

verses.english: But he said to him, "Let the dead bury their own dead; but you, go and proclaim the kingdom of God."
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ· Ἄφες τοὺς νεκροὺς θάψαι τοὺς ἑαυτῶν νεκρούς, σὺ δὲ ἀπελθὼν διάγγελλε τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.english: Another said, "I will follow you, Lord; but first let me say farewell to those at my home."
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ καὶ ἕτερος· Ἀκολουθήσω σοι, κύριε· πρῶτον δὲ ἐπίτρεψόν μοι ἀποτάξασθαι τοῖς εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου.

verses.english: Jesus said to him, "No one who puts his hand to the plough and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God."
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐδεὶς ἐπιβαλὼν τὴν χεῖρα ἐπ’ ἄροτρον καὶ βλέπων εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω εὔθετός ἐστιν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ.

notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.21.6–7: Peter answers "Tu es Christus", Jesus imposes silence, and gives as the reason that "the son of man must suffer many things, be rejected by the elders and scribes and priests, be killed, and rise after the third day". Epiphanius, sch. 16 quotes the prediction in Greek with μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ("after three days") for canonical Luke's "on the third day"; that form is printed (D and the Old Latin have it, as does Mark 8:31). 9:18–19 are read in the Dialogue of Adamantius (84,1–4); Roth counts them as attested. NA27 reads λέγουσιν οἱ ὄχλοι at 9:18 (SBLGNT has a different order).

Tertullian, Marc. 4.21.8–12 quotes 9:24 ("whoever wants to save his life will lose it…") and 9:26 ("whoever is ashamed of me, I will be ashamed of him"), and argues at length that only a Christ with a real birth and flesh could be a cause of shame. His quotation of 9:26 lacks "and my words" (also lacking in D and some Old Latin and Old Syriac witnesses) and the coming "in his glory" (9:26b). One witness; NA27 printed and the evidence noted. 9:23, 9:25 and 9:27 are not cited and are printed in grey.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.22.1–16; Epiphanius, sch. 17–18. Both witnesses give the voice as "This is my beloved son" (ἀγαπητός; "filius meus dilectus"), and NA27 cites Marcion for it with A C* W, the Byzantine text and the Old Latin; it is printed for canonical Luke's "my chosen". Tertullian says that Marcion did not want Moses shown "speaking with the Lord, but standing" (4.22.16). Roth takes this to mean 9:31b ("they spoke of his departure, which he was to fulfil at Jerusalem") was not in the text, and it is not printed. Epiphanius' copy did have them "talking with him" (9:30), so the copies may have differed on the conversation. 9:36 is not cited and is printed in grey.

Reception and interpretation. For Tertullian the scene proves that Jesus belongs with the law and the prophets: "he would not show them in conversation, a sign of familiarity, nor in a share of his glory" if he had come to destroy them (4.22.2). The Marcionite reading took the voice ("listen to him") as transferring authority away from Moses and Elijah (4.22.1). The attested text shows Jesus with Moses and Elijah in glory and the voice naming him son. It does not itself say whether their authority is confirmed or ended.

Epiphanius, sch. 19 quotes the father's words and the reply "to them": »ὦ γενεὰ ἄπιστος, ἕως πότε ἀνέξομαι ὑμῶν;«. Tertullian quotes the reply twice (4.23.1–2), "O genitura incredula, quousque ero apud vos? quousque sustinebo vos?". Neither has "and perverse" (καὶ διεστραμμένη), which canonical Luke shares with Matthew 17:17; the shorter address is Mark's (9:19). The words are absent from two witnesses' quotations and are not printed (METHOD §5.3). The witnesses differ on the rest: Tertullian has two "how long" clauses, as in Matthew and Mark, and Epiphanius one. Their copies were harmonized differently, a point made by Williams and BeDuhn (working document §2.2). 9:37–39 and 9:42–43a are not cited and are printed in grey.

Epiphanius, sch. 20 quotes the second passion prediction (9:44). Tertullian, Marc. 4.23.4 sets Jesus' love of children against the Antitheses' example of Elisha and the bears (2 Kgs 2:23–24). NA27 reads ὃς ἐὰν δέξηται at 9:48 (SBLGNT ὃς ἄν). 9:43b and 9:45 are not cited and are printed in grey. 9:49–50 (the strange exorcist) form a separate paragraph that no witness cites, and are not printed.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.23.8–9: against the Creator's fire called down by Elijah (2 Kgs 1:10–12) stands Christ's leniency, "rebuking the disciples who wanted the same punishment for that village of the Samaritans". This attests 9:52, which Roth lists as unattested, and 9:54–55. Two longer readings of canonical manuscripts, "as Elijah did" (9:54) and "you do not know of what spirit you are…" (9:55–56), are not attested for this text. Tertullian brings in Elijah himself, as the Antitheses did. 9:51, 9:53 and 9:56 are not cited and are printed in grey.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.23.9–11 attests all three exchanges, quoting "Let the dead bury their dead, but you go and proclaim the kingdom of God". He argues that the reply keeps the law forbidding priests and Nazirites contact with the dead (Lev 21:1; Num 6:6–7). NA27 prints [κύριε] at 9:59 and [πρὸς αὐτόν] at 9:62 in brackets; both are printed.

Interpretation. The attested text predicts suffering, death and being raised "after three days", and Tertullian takes the prediction as the Creator's prophecy fulfilled (4.21.7). In 9:60 he reads the call to leave the dead to bury their dead as the Nazirite and priestly rule applied to those devoted to the kingdom (4.23.10). Hegesippus' report that James lived as a Nazirite, which the library uses (Carriers of Living Water §3.2), concerns the same pattern of consecration; whether the saying was read that way in the community behind the text cannot be shown from the witnesses.

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 8
chapters.preamble: The mission of the seventy and what follows from it. Jesus sends out seventy others, two by two, with the instructions Tertullian reads as the Creator's own: no sandals, no greetings on the road, peace to the house, "the worker deserves his wages", and the dust wiped off against a town that refuses them, "yet know this: the kingdom of God has come near". Whoever rejects them rejects him; he gives them authority over snakes and scorpions. He then thanks the "Lord of heaven" that what was hidden from the wise has been revealed to little children, and says that no one knows who the Father is except the son. To a lawyer who asks what he must do to inherit life ("life", not "eternal life", as Tertullian points out) he answers with the command to love God, and "do this and you will live". Canonical Luke's judgement on Sodom and the woes on the Galilean towns, "I saw Satan fall", the parable of the Samaritan and the visit to Martha and Mary are not cited by either witness and are not printed.

verses.english: After this the Lord appointed seventy others and sent them on ahead of him, two by two, into every town and place where he himself was about to come.
verses.greek: Μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα ἀνέδειξεν ὁ κύριος ἑτέρους ἑβδομήκοντα καὶ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς ἀνὰ δύο δύο πρὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ εἰς πᾶσαν πόλιν καὶ τόπον οὗ ἤμελλεν αὐτὸς ἔρχεσθαι.

verses.english: He said to them, "The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few; so ask the Lord of the harvest to send out workers into his harvest.
verses.greek: ἔλεγεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Ὁ μὲν θερισμὸς πολύς, οἱ δὲ ἐργάται ὀλίγοι· δεήθητε οὖν τοῦ κυρίου τοῦ θερισμοῦ ὅπως ἐργάτας ἐκβάλῃ εἰς τὸν θερισμὸν αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: Go; behold, I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.
verses.greek: ὑπάγετε· ἰδοὺ ἀποστέλλω ὑμᾶς ὡς ἄρνας ἐν μέσῳ λύκων.

verses.english: Carry no purse, no bag, no sandals; and greet no one on the road.
verses.greek: μὴ βαστάζετε βαλλάντιον, μὴ πήραν, μὴ ὑποδήματα, καὶ μηδένα κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ἀσπάσησθε.

verses.english: Whatever house you enter, first say, "Peace to this house."
verses.greek: εἰς ἣν δ’ ἂν εἰσέλθητε οἰκίαν πρῶτον λέγετε· Εἰρήνη τῷ οἴκῳ τούτῳ.

verses.english: And if a son of peace is there, your peace will rest on him; if not, it will return to you.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐὰν ἐκεῖ ᾖ υἱὸς εἰρήνης, ἐπαναπαήσεται ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν· εἰ δὲ μή γε, ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ἀνακάμψει.

verses.english: Stay in that same house, eating and drinking what they provide, for the worker deserves his wages. Do not move from house to house.
verses.greek: ἐν αὐτῇ δὲ τῇ οἰκίᾳ μένετε, ἐσθίοντες καὶ πίνοντες τὰ παρ’ αὐτῶν, ἄξιος γὰρ ὁ ἐργάτης τοῦ μισθοῦ αὐτοῦ. μὴ μεταβαίνετε ἐξ οἰκίας εἰς οἰκίαν.

verses.english: Whenever you enter a town and they welcome you, eat what is set before you;
verses.greek: καὶ εἰς ἣν ἂν πόλιν εἰσέρχησθε καὶ δέχωνται ὑμᾶς, ἐσθίετε τὰ παρατιθέμενα ὑμῖν,

verses.english: heal the sick in it and say to them, "The kingdom of God has come near to you."
verses.greek: καὶ θεραπεύετε τοὺς ἐν αὐτῇ ἀσθενεῖς, καὶ λέγετε αὐτοῖς· Ἤγγικεν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.english: But whenever you enter a town and they do not welcome you, go out into its streets and say,
verses.greek: εἰς ἣν δ’ ἂν πόλιν εἰσέλθητε καὶ μὴ δέχωνται ὑμᾶς, ἐξελθόντες εἰς τὰς πλατείας αὐτῆς εἴπατε·

verses.english: "Even the dust of your town that clings to our feet we wipe off against you. Yet know this: the kingdom of God has come near."
verses.greek: Καὶ τὸν κονιορτὸν τὸν κολληθέντα ἡμῖν ἐκ τῆς πόλεως ὑμῶν εἰς τοὺς πόδας ἀπομασσόμεθα ὑμῖν· πλὴν τοῦτο γινώσκετε ὅτι ἤγγικεν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.english: Whoever listens to you listens to me, and whoever rejects you rejects me; and whoever rejects me rejects the one who sent me."
verses.greek: Ὁ ἀκούων ὑμῶν ἐμοῦ ἀκούει, καὶ ὁ ἀθετῶν ὑμᾶς ἐμὲ ἀθετεῖ· ὁ δὲ ἐμὲ ἀθετῶν ἀθετεῖ τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με.

verses.english: The seventy returned with joy, saying, "Lord, even the daimons submit to us in your name!"
verses.greek: Ὑπέστρεψαν δὲ οἱ ἑβδομήκοντα μετὰ χαρᾶς λέγοντες· Κύριε, καὶ τὰ δαιμόνια ὑποτάσσεται ἡμῖν ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου.

verses.english: Behold, I have given you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy; and nothing will harm you.
verses.greek: ἰδοὺ δέδωκα ὑμῖν τὴν ἐξουσίαν τοῦ πατεῖν ἐπάνω ὄφεων καὶ σκορπίων, καὶ ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ ἐχθροῦ, καὶ οὐδὲν ὑμᾶς οὐ μὴ ἀδικήσῃ.

verses.english: Nevertheless, do not rejoice in this, that the spirits submit to you; rejoice rather that your names are written in the heavens."
verses.greek: πλὴν ἐν τούτῳ μὴ χαίρετε ὅτι τὰ πνεύματα ὑμῖν ὑποτάσσεται, χαίρετε δὲ ὅτι τὰ ὀνόματα ὑμῶν ἐγγέγραπται ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.

verses.english: In that same hour he rejoiced in the holy spirit and said, "I thank you, Lord of heaven, that what was hidden from the wise and understanding you have revealed to little children. Yes, Father, for so it was pleasing in your sight.
verses.greek: Ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἠγαλλιάσατο ἐν τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ καὶ εἶπεν· Εὐχαριστῶ σοι, κύριε τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, ὅτι ἅτινα ἦν κρυπτὰ σοφοῖς καὶ συνετοῖς ἀπεκάλυψας νηπίοις· ναὶ ὁ πατήρ, ὅτι οὕτως εὐδοκία ἐγένετο ἔμπροσθέν σου.

verses.english: All things have been handed over to me by my Father; and no one knows who the Father is except the son, and who the son is except the Father, and anyone to whom the son chooses to reveal him."
verses.greek: πάντα μοι παρεδόθη ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρός μου, καὶ οὐδεὶς γινώσκει τίς ἐστιν ὁ πατὴρ εἰ μὴ ὁ υἱός, καὶ τίς ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς εἰ μὴ ὁ πατὴρ καὶ ᾧ ἐὰν βούληται ὁ υἱὸς ἀποκαλύψαι.

verses.english: Then turning to the disciples he said privately, "Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.
verses.greek: Καὶ στραφεὶς πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς κατ’ ἰδίαν εἶπεν· Μακάριοι οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ οἱ βλέποντες ἃ βλέπετε.

verses.english: For I tell you that many prophets and kings wanted to see what you see, and did not see it, and to hear what you hear, and did not hear it."
verses.greek: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι πολλοὶ προφῆται καὶ βασιλεῖς ἠθέλησαν ἰδεῖν ἃ ὑμεῖς βλέπετε καὶ οὐκ εἶδαν, καὶ ἀκοῦσαι ἃ ἀκούετε καὶ οὐκ ἤκουσαν.

verses.english: And behold, a lawyer stood up to test him, saying, "Teacher, what must I do to inherit life?"
verses.greek: Καὶ ἰδοὺ νομικός τις ἀνέστη ἐκπειράζων αὐτὸν λέγων· Διδάσκαλε, τί ποιήσας ζωὴν κληρονομήσω;

verses.english: He said to him, "What is written in the law? How do you read it?"
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἐν τῷ νόμῳ τί γέγραπται; πῶς ἀναγινώσκεις;

verses.english: He answered, "You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your strength, and with all your mind; and your neighbour as yourself."
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ἀγαπήσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ψυχῇ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ἰσχύϊ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ διανοίᾳ σου, καὶ τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν.

verses.english: He said to him, "You have answered rightly; do this, and you will live."
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ· Ὀρθῶς ἀπεκρίθης· τοῦτο ποίει καὶ ζήσῃ.

notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.24.1–7 follows the instructions in order: seventy others appointed, sent into towns, no sandals, no greetings on the road (as Elisha told Gehazi, 2 Kgs 4:29), peace to the house (as Elisha to the Shunammite, 2 Kgs 4:26), "the worker deserves his wages" (as the law on the ox, Deut 25:4), the kingdom announced as "near", and the words to a town that refuses them. The number is seventy: Tertullian sets the seventy beside the seventy palms of Elim as he sets the twelve beside its twelve springs (Exod 15:27). NA27 prints "seventy [two]" with the second word bracketed; it is not printed here (METHOD §5.7). 10:2–3 and 10:6 are not cited and are printed in grey.

Sodom "on that day" and the woes on Chorazin, Bethsaida and Capernaum. Tertullian goes from 10:11 to 10:16 and argues, at length, that the dust saying implies a judgement: "if he does not command it as a threat, he commands it in vain" (4.24.7). The verses that state the judgement in so many words, and name the Creator's judgement on Sodom, would have ended the argument. He does not cite them. They are classed "unattested, probably absent".

Tertullian quotes "Whoever rejects you rejects me" (4.24.8) and asks who will give power "to tread on snakes and scorpions" if not the Lord of all creatures (4.24.9). He reads the snakes and scorpions as the spiritual powers of wickedness and their prince as the serpent and dragon of Ps 91:13 and Isa 27:1 (4.24.10). "I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven" (10:18), which would have suited that reading, is not cited and is not printed. 10:17 and 10:20 are printed in grey. "Seventy" at 10:17 follows 10:1.

Both witnesses quote the thanksgiving. Epiphanius, sch. 22: "I thank you, Lord of heaven"; the text "did not have 'and of the earth', nor did it have 'Father'", but it did have "Yes, Father" further on. Tertullian, Marc. 4.25.1: "Gratias ago, et confiteor, domine caeli, quod ea quae erant abscondita sapientibus et prudentibus, revelaveris parvulis." The address without "and of the earth" is also the reading of 𝔓45. In Tertullian the hiding has no stated subject: what was hidden, God has revealed. His later reply that the Marcionite God, revealing what the Creator had hidden, would have been doing the Creator's work (4.25.6) presupposes that wording. The Greek printed is Roth's retroversion; the sense is attested, the exact words are not. Tertullian's "et confiteor" (= canonical ἐξομολογοῦμαι) is in his text only and is not printed.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.25.10 quotes the saying with the Father first: "No one knows who the Father is except the son, and who the son is except the Father" (canonical Luke has the son first). The order is attested also by the Dialogue of Adamantius and by Eznik, and is found in some manuscripts and fathers (Roth). Tertullian comments: "and so Christ preached an unknown God" — the Marcionite reading of the saying, which he answers from Isaiah ("Israel did not know me", Isa 1:3). The words in brackets after the quotation in the manuscripts of Tertullian give Matthew's wording and are a copyist's addition.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.25.14: "In the gospel of truth the lawyer asks, 'What must I do to obtain eternal life?' In the heretical one only 'life' is set down, with no mention of 'eternal'." This is one of the few places where Tertullian states a difference between the two texts, and in 4.25.18 he allows that "ours" may have added the word. The text printed reads "inherit life". Epiphanius, sch. 23 quotes Jesus' question "What is written in the law?" and his reply "You have said rightly; do this and you will live" (10:26, 28). Tertullian's quotation of the command (10:27) has three clauses (heart, soul, strength) and no neighbour clause; NA27 cites his Marcion for the lack of "with all your mind". These are noted, not adopted (one witness).

The parable of the Samaritan (10:29–37) and the visit to Martha and Mary (10:38–42). In both witnesses the exchange with the lawyer ends at 10:28; Tertullian goes on to 11:1 and Epiphanius to 11:5. For the parable, silence counts: it expounds the law's own command of love, the point Tertullian was arguing ("he set before him the head of the law", 4.25.15), and it would have served him. It is classed "unattested, probably absent". The Martha and Mary passage touches nothing either father argues, so their silence shows nothing; it is "unattested, undetermined" and, as a paragraph with no attested verse, is not printed (METHOD §4.3).

Interpretation. In the attested text the way to "life" is the command of Deuteronomy 6:5, and Jesus' answer is "do this, and you will live" (cf. Lev 18:5). Tertullian takes the shorter question to concern the long life the law promises (4.25.14); the text itself does not say which life is meant. What it does show is a teacher who answers a question about life with the law's first command and a call to do it — the pattern of 6:46 and 8:21 in this reconstruction, and of the Epistle of James ("be doers of the word", Jas 1:22).

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 9
chapters.preamble: Prayer, the finger of God, and the woes. Asked by a disciple to teach them to pray, Jesus gives a prayer that in this text asks first for the holy spirit, then for the kingdom, for "your bread", forgiveness, and not to be brought into temptation (Tertullian, Marc. 4.26.3–5; Origen). Its parables end with the Father who gives the holy spirit to those who ask. Accused of casting out daimons by Beelzebul, Jesus answers that he does it "by the finger of God", the words the Egyptian magicians used before Moses (Exod 8:19). To a generation seeking a sign he says that no sign will be given to it; this text has no sign of Jonah and no Nineveh or queen of the south (Epiphanius, sch. 25). At a Pharisee's table come the sayings on the inside and the outside of the cup and the woes on Pharisees and lawyers; the Pharisees pass over "the calling and the love of God". The saying of "the wisdom of God" about the blood of the prophets is not in this text (sch. 28).

verses.english: Once he was praying in a certain place, and when he had finished, one of his disciples said to him, "Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples."
verses.greek: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐν τόπῳ τινὶ προσευχόμενον, ὡς ἐπαύσατο, εἶπέν τις τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ πρὸς αὐτόν· Κύριε, δίδαξον ἡμᾶς προσεύχεσθαι, καθὼς καὶ Ἰωάννης ἐδίδαξεν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: He said to them, "When you pray, say: Father, may your holy spirit come; may your kingdom come;
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ὅταν προσεύχησθε, λέγετε· Πάτερ, ἐλθέτω τὸ πνεῦμά σου τὸ ἅγιον· ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία σου·

verses.english: give us each day your bread for the coming day;
verses.greek: τὸν ἄρτον σου τὸν ἐπιούσιον δίδου ἡμῖν τὸ καθ’ ἡμέραν·

verses.english: and forgive us our sins, for we ourselves forgive everyone indebted to us; and do not bring us into temptation."
verses.greek: καὶ ἄφες ἡμῖν τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν, καὶ γὰρ αὐτοὶ ἀφίομεν παντὶ ὀφείλοντι ἡμῖν· καὶ μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς πειρασμόν.

verses.english: And he said to them, "Which of you has a friend, and goes to him at midnight and says to him, 'Friend, lend me three loaves,
verses.greek: Καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τίς ἐξ ὑμῶν ἕξει φίλον καὶ πορεύσεται πρὸς αὐτὸν μεσονυκτίου καὶ εἴπῃ αὐτῷ· Φίλε, χρῆσόν μοι τρεῖς ἄρτους,

verses.english: for a friend of mine has arrived from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him';
verses.greek: ἐπειδὴ φίλος μου παρεγένετο ἐξ ὁδοῦ πρός με καὶ οὐκ ἔχω ὃ παραθήσω αὐτῷ·

verses.english: and he answers from inside, 'Do not bother me; the door is already shut, and my children are with me in bed; I cannot get up and give you anything'?
verses.greek: κἀκεῖνος ἔσωθεν ἀποκριθεὶς εἴπῃ· Μή μοι κόπους πάρεχε· ἤδη ἡ θύρα κέκλεισται, καὶ τὰ παιδία μου μετ’ ἐμοῦ εἰς τὴν κοίτην εἰσίν· οὐ δύναμαι ἀναστὰς δοῦναί σοι.

verses.english: I tell you, even if he will not get up and give him anything because he is his friend, yet because of his persistence he will rise and give him whatever he needs.
verses.greek: λέγω ὑμῖν, εἰ καὶ οὐ δώσει αὐτῷ ἀναστὰς διὰ τὸ εἶναι φίλον αὐτοῦ, διά γε τὴν ἀναίδειαν αὐτοῦ ἐγερθεὶς δώσει αὐτῷ ὅσων χρῄζει.

verses.english: So I say to you: ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
verses.greek: Κἀγὼ ὑμῖν λέγω, αἰτεῖτε, καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν· ζητεῖτε, καὶ εὑρήσετε· κρούετε, καὶ ἀνοιγήσεται ὑμῖν·

verses.english: For everyone who asks receives, and the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.
verses.greek: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ αἰτῶν λαμβάνει, καὶ ὁ ζητῶν εὑρίσκει, καὶ τῷ κρούοντι ἀνοιγήσεται.

verses.english: What father among you, if his son asks for a fish, will give him a snake instead of a fish?
verses.greek: τίνα δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν τὸν πατέρα αἰτήσει ὁ υἱὸς ἰχθύν, καὶ ἀντὶ ἰχθύος ὄφιν αὐτῷ ἐπιδώσει;

verses.english: Or if he asks for an egg, will give him a scorpion?
verses.greek: ἢ καὶ αἰτήσει ᾠόν, ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ σκορπίον;

verses.english: If you then, who are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will the Father from heaven give the holy spirit to those who ask him!"
verses.greek: εἰ οὖν ὑμεῖς πονηροὶ ὑπάρχοντες οἴδατε δόματα ἀγαθὰ διδόναι τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὁ πατὴρ ὁ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ δώσει πνεῦμα ἅγιον τοῖς αἰτοῦσιν αὐτόν.

verses.english: Now he was casting out a daimon, and it was mute. When the daimon had gone out, the mute man spoke, and the crowds were amazed.
verses.greek: Καὶ ἦν ἐκβάλλων δαιμόνιον καὶ αὐτὸ ἦν κωφόν· ἐγένετο δὲ τοῦ δαιμονίου ἐξελθόντος ἐλάλησεν ὁ κωφός. καὶ ἐθαύμασαν οἱ ὄχλοι·

verses.english: But some of them said, "He casts out the daimons by Beelzebul, the ruler of the daimons."
verses.greek: τινὲς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶπον· Ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ τῷ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια·

verses.english: Others, to test him, demanded from him a sign from heaven.
verses.greek: ἕτεροι δὲ πειράζοντες σημεῖον ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐζήτουν παρ’ αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: But he knew their thoughts and said to them, "Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and house falls on house.
verses.greek: αὐτὸς δὲ εἰδὼς αὐτῶν τὰ διανοήματα εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πᾶσα βασιλεία ἐφ’ ἑαυτὴν διαμερισθεῖσα ἐρημοῦται, καὶ οἶκος ἐπὶ οἶκον πίπτει.

verses.english: If Satan also is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? For you say that I cast out the daimons by Beelzebul.
verses.greek: εἰ δὲ καὶ ὁ Σατανᾶς ἐφ’ ἑαυτὸν διεμερίσθη, πῶς σταθήσεται ἡ βασιλεία αὐτοῦ; ὅτι λέγετε ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐκβάλλειν με τὰ δαιμόνια.

verses.english: And if I cast out the daimons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.
verses.greek: εἰ δὲ ἐγὼ ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, οἱ υἱοὶ ὑμῶν ἐν τίνι ἐκβάλλουσιν; διὰ τοῦτο αὐτοὶ ὑμῶν κριταὶ ἔσονται.

verses.english: But if I cast out the daimons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
verses.greek: εἰ δὲ ἐν δακτύλῳ θεοῦ ἐγὼ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, ἄρα ἔφθασεν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.english: When a strong man, fully armed, guards his own court, his possessions are safe;
verses.greek: ὅταν ὁ ἰσχυρὸς καθωπλισμένος φυλάσσῃ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ αὐλήν, ἐν εἰρήνῃ ἐστὶν τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ·

verses.english: but when one stronger than he attacks him and overcomes him, he takes away the armour in which he trusted and divides his plunder.
verses.greek: ἐπὰν δὲ ἰσχυρότερος αὐτοῦ ἐπελθὼν νικήσῃ αὐτόν, τὴν πανοπλίαν αὐτοῦ αἴρει ἐφ’ ᾗ ἐπεποίθει, καὶ τὰ σκῦλα αὐτοῦ διαδίδωσιν.

verses.english: Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.
verses.greek: ὁ μὴ ὢν μετ’ ἐμοῦ κατ’ ἐμοῦ ἐστιν, καὶ ὁ μὴ συνάγων μετ’ ἐμοῦ σκορπίζει.

verses.english: While he was saying this, a woman in the crowd raised her voice and said to him, "Blessed is the womb that bore you and the breasts that you sucked!"
verses.greek: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ λέγειν αὐτὸν ταῦτα ἐπάρασά τις φωνὴν γυνὴ ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Μακαρία ἡ κοιλία ἡ βαστάσασά σε καὶ μαστοὶ οὓς ἐθήλασας·

verses.english: But he said, "Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and keep it!"
verses.greek: αὐτὸς δὲ εἶπεν· Μενοῦν μακάριοι οἱ ἀκούοντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ φυλάσσοντες.

verses.english: As the crowds were increasing, he began to say, "This generation is an evil generation; it seeks a sign, and no sign will be given to it."
verses.greek: Τῶν δὲ ὄχλων ἐπαθροιζομένων ἤρξατο λέγειν· Ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη γενεὰ πονηρά ἐστιν· σημεῖον ζητεῖ, καὶ σημεῖον οὐ δοθήσεται αὐτῇ.

verses.english: No one lights a lamp and puts it in a cellar or under a basket, but on a lampstand, so that those who come in may see the light.
verses.greek: Οὐδεὶς λύχνον ἅψας εἰς κρύπτην τίθησιν οὐδὲ ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν, ἵνα οἱ εἰσπορευόμενοι τὸ φῶς βλέπωσιν.

verses.english: While he was speaking, a Pharisee asked him to dine with him; so he went in and reclined at table.
verses.greek: Ἐν δὲ τῷ λαλῆσαι ἐρωτᾷ αὐτὸν Φαρισαῖος ὅπως ἀριστήσῃ παρ’ αὐτῷ· εἰσελθὼν δὲ ἀνέπεσεν.

verses.english: The Pharisee began to debate within himself, saying, "Why did he not first wash before the meal?"
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ Φαρισαῖος ἤρξατο διακρινόμενος ἐν ἑαυτῷ λέγειν διὰ τί οὐ πρῶτον ἐβαπτίσθη πρὸ τοῦ ἀρίστου.

verses.english: But the Lord said to him, "Now you Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and of the dish, but inside you are full of greed and wickedness.
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ κύριος πρὸς αὐτόν· Νῦν ὑμεῖς οἱ Φαρισαῖοι τὸ ἔξωθεν τοῦ ποτηρίου καὶ τοῦ πίνακος καθαρίζετε, τὸ δὲ ἔσωθεν ὑμῶν γέμει ἁρπαγῆς καὶ πονηρίας.

verses.english: Fools! Did not the one who made the outside make the inside also?
verses.greek: ἄφρονες, οὐχ ὁ ποιήσας τὸ ἔξωθεν καὶ τὸ ἔσωθεν ἐποίησεν;

verses.english: But give as alms what is within, and behold, everything is clean for you.
verses.greek: πλὴν τὰ ἐνόντα δότε ἐλεημοσύνην, καὶ ἰδοὺ πάντα καθαρὰ ὑμῖν ἐστιν.

verses.english: But woe to you Pharisees! For you tithe mint and rue and every herb, and pass over the calling and the love of God. These you ought to have done, without neglecting the others.
verses.greek: Ἀλλὰ οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς Φαρισαίοις, ὅτι ἀποδεκατοῦτε τὸ ἡδύοσμον καὶ τὸ πήγανον καὶ πᾶν λάχανον, καὶ παρέρχεσθε τὴν κλῆσιν καὶ τὴν ἀγάπην τοῦ θεοῦ· ταῦτα δὲ ἔδει ποιῆσαι κἀκεῖνα μὴ παρεῖναι.

verses.english: Woe to you Pharisees! For you love the best seat in the synagogues and greetings in the market-places.
verses.greek: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς Φαρισαίοις, ὅτι ἀγαπᾶτε τὴν πρωτοκαθεδρίαν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ τοὺς ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς.

verses.english: Woe to you! For you are like unmarked graves, and people walk over them without knowing it."
verses.greek: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, ὅτι ἐστὲ ὡς τὰ μνημεῖα τὰ ἄδηλα, καὶ οἱ ἄνθρωποι οἱ περιπατοῦντες ἐπάνω οὐκ οἴδασιν.

verses.english: One of the lawyers answered him, "Teacher, in saying this you insult us too."
verses.greek: Ἀποκριθεὶς δέ τις τῶν νομικῶν λέγει αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, ταῦτα λέγων καὶ ἡμᾶς ὑβρίζεις.

verses.english: And he said, "Woe to you lawyers also! For you load people with burdens hard to bear, and you yourselves do not touch the burdens with one of your fingers.
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Καὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς νομικοῖς οὐαί, ὅτι φορτίζετε τοὺς ἀνθρώπους φορτία δυσβάστακτα, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἑνὶ τῶν δακτύλων ὑμῶν οὐ προσψαύετε τοῖς φορτίοις.

verses.english: Woe to you! For you build the tombs of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.
verses.greek: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, ὅτι οἰκοδομεῖτε τὰ μνημεῖα τῶν προφητῶν οἱ δὲ πατέρες ὑμῶν ἀπέκτειναν αὐτούς.

verses.english: So you are witnesses and approve of the deeds of your fathers; for they killed them, and you build.
verses.greek: ἄρα μάρτυρές ἐστε καὶ συνευδοκεῖτε τοῖς ἔργοις τῶν πατέρων ὑμῶν, ὅτι αὐτοὶ μὲν ἀπέκτειναν αὐτοὺς ὑμεῖς δὲ οἰκοδομεῖτε.

verses.english: Woe to you lawyers! For you have taken away the key of knowledge; you did not enter yourselves, and you hindered those who were entering."
verses.greek: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς νομικοῖς, ὅτι ἤρατε τὴν κλεῖδα τῆς γνώσεως· αὐτοὶ οὐκ εἰσήλθατε καὶ τοὺς εἰσερχομένους ἐκωλύσατε.

notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.26.1–5 does not quote the prayer. He turns each petition into a question about which God it is addressed to, in the order of the prayer, and then says "in this order" (hoc ordine): "To whom shall I say, Father?… From whom shall I ask the holy spirit?… Whose kingdom shall I wish to come?… Who will give me daily bread?… Who will forgive me my sins?… Who will not let us be led into temptation?" There is no question about the hallowing of the name. The text therefore asked for the holy spirit where canonical Luke has "hallowed be your name", and kept "your kingdom come". Tertullian does not give the wording of the request for the spirit. The Greek printed takes the form of the only Greek witnesses with such a petition in Luke (minuscules 700 and 162, Gregory of Nyssa), shortened to what Tertullian attests. In those witnesses it replaces "your kingdom come"; here it stands beside it. Origen quotes the bread petition of "those from Marcion" in Greek: "your bread" (τὸν ἄρτον σου), not "our bread". He asks them "what is the bread of God?" ἐπιούσιος is translated "for the coming day"; Tertullian has "daily" (cotidianum).

notes.term: The holy spirit asked and given (11:2, 11:13)
notes.explanation: Interpretation. In this text the prayer opens with a request for the holy spirit, and the teaching that follows ends with the Father who will "give the holy spirit to those who ask him" (11:13; Tertullian 4.26.10). The unit begins and ends with the spirit. The bread asked for is the Father's ("your bread"), and Origen's question to the Marcionites, "what is the bread of God?", shows that they read it as more than food. This is the reception, and the text does not settle that reading. What the text itself shows is a prayer centred on receiving from the Father. The library reads such receiving as influx into a vessel (The River and the Vessel).

Epiphanius, sch. 24 quotes 11:5, 11:9a and 11:11–13 in one scholion; Tertullian, Marc. 4.26.5–10 alludes to the friend at midnight, the door already shut with the children in bed, the request granted because of persistence, the asking, seeking and knocking, and the snake and scorpion. Neither witness has the pair "bread and stone" that most manuscripts add at 11:11 (it is also absent in 𝔓45, 𝔓75 and B). 11:6 and 11:10 are not cited and are printed in grey.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.26.10–12 quotes "If I cast out daimons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out?" and "If I by the finger of God cast out daimons, has the kingdom of God not come near to you?" He points out that the Egyptian magicians called the Creator's power "the finger of God" (Exod 8:19), and that the stronger man of the parable overcomes the prince of daimons. NA27 prints [καὶ αὐτὸ ἦν] at 11:14 and [ἐγώ] at 11:20 in brackets; both are printed (SBLGNT omits them). 11:16–17 and 11:23 are not cited and are printed in grey. The return of the unclean spirit (11:24–26), a paragraph that no witness cites, is not printed.

Epiphanius, sch. 25: "he cut out what is about Jonah the prophet; for he had 'this generation — no sign will be given to it'; he did not have what is about Nineveh and the queen of the south and Solomon." Tertullian: Christ "does not give a sign to those who ask" (4.27.1). The saying in this text ends "no sign will be given to it". Canonical Luke adds "except the sign of Jonah" and the sayings on the Ninevites and the queen of the south (11:30–32, Matthew 12:39–42). The verbs "he cut" are Epiphanius' charge. What they report as content is that the words were not there.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.27.2–5. The Pharisee "was debating within himself why he had not first been washed before reclining, according to the law". That is the reading of codex D and the Old Latin, and it is printed in D's Greek. Canonical Luke has the Pharisee "amazed". Jesus' reply on the outside and inside of the cup, "Did not the one who made the outside make the inside also?", is glossed by Tertullian as flesh and soul made by one God. At 11:42 both witnesses read that the Pharisees pass over "the calling (κλῆσις) and the love of God", not "justice (κρίσις) and the love of God"; Tertullian repeats "calling" in 4.27.6. The reading is printed. 11:44 is not cited and is printed in grey.

notes.term: Woes on the lawyers (11:45–52; 11:49–51 not printed)
notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.27.6–9; Epiphanius, sch. 27–28. The lawyers load others with burdens hard to bear; they build the tombs of the prophets their fathers killed; they have taken the key of knowledge (Tertullian: "the interpretation of the law"). Epiphanius states that the text did not have the saying "Therefore the wisdom of God said, 'I will send them prophets…'" or the blood of the prophets from Abel to Zechariah "required of this generation" (11:49–51). At 11:48 Tertullian's comment ("they testified that they did not consent to the deeds of their fathers") agrees with the reading of D, "you testify that you do not approve"; it is not a quotation and is recorded, not adopted. 11:45 is not cited and is printed in grey. 11:53–54 form a paragraph that no witness cites and are not printed.

Interpretation. In the attested text the charge against the Pharisees is that they tithe herbs and pass over "the calling and the love of God". Tertullian reads "calling" as God calling Israel out of Egypt and "love" as the first commandment (Deut 6:5), quoted in that form (4.27.4). The pairing fits the reconstruction's earlier sayings: the lawyer is answered with the command to love God (10:27). It also fits a criticism of religious leaders made from within the law, for neglecting what the law puts first.

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 10
chapters.preamble: Fear and trust. Jesus warns his disciples against the leaven of the Pharisees and tells them not to fear those who can only kill the body, but the one who has authority to cast into Gehenna. Whoever acknowledges him will be acknowledged "before God" (this text has no angels in 12:8–9), and the holy spirit will teach them what to say. He refuses to divide an inheritance and tells of the rich fool. He tells them not to worry about food and clothing, but to seek the kingdom of God, which "the Father" is pleased to give them. Then come the parables of watchfulness: servants waiting for their master to return from a wedding "in the evening watch", the thief, and the steward. He has come to cast fire on the earth and to bring division, and he calls the crowds hypocrites who read the face of heaven and earth but not the present time. The five sparrows (12:6), which Epiphanius says the text lacked, and the saying on God clothing the grass (12:28a) are not printed.

verses.english: Meanwhile, when the crowd had gathered in thousands, so that they trampled on one another, he began to say to his disciples first, "Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
verses.greek: Ἐν οἷς ἐπισυναχθεισῶν τῶν μυριάδων τοῦ ὄχλου, ὥστε καταπατεῖν ἀλλήλους, ἤρξατο λέγειν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ πρῶτον· Προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης, ἥτις ἐστὶν ὑπόκρισις, τῶν Φαρισαίων.

verses.english: Nothing is covered up that will not be revealed, or hidden that will not be known.
verses.greek: οὐδὲν δὲ συγκεκαλυμμένον ἐστὶν ὃ οὐκ ἀποκαλυφθήσεται, καὶ κρυπτὸν ὃ οὐ γνωσθήσεται.

verses.english: Therefore whatever you have said in the dark will be heard in the light, and what you have whispered in private rooms will be proclaimed on the housetops.
verses.greek: ἀνθ’ ὧν ὅσα ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ εἴπατε ἐν τῷ φωτὶ ἀκουσθήσεται, καὶ ὃ πρὸς τὸ οὖς ἐλαλήσατε ἐν τοῖς ταμείοις κηρυχθήσεται ἐπὶ τῶν δωμάτων.

verses.english: I tell you, my friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that can do nothing more.
verses.greek: Λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν τοῖς φίλοις μου, μὴ φοβηθῆτε ἀπὸ τῶν ἀποκτεινόντων τὸ σῶμα καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα μὴ ἐχόντων περισσότερόν τι ποιῆσαι.

verses.english: But I will show you whom to fear: fear the one who, after he has killed, has authority to cast into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear him.
verses.greek: ὑποδείξω δὲ ὑμῖν τίνα φοβηθῆτε· φοβήθητε τὸν μετὰ τὸ ἀποκτεῖναι ἔχοντα ἐξουσίαν βαλεῖν εἰς γέενναν· ναί, λέγω ὑμῖν, τοῦτον φοβήθητε.

verses.english: I tell you, everyone who acknowledges me before people, the son of man also will acknowledge before God;
verses.greek: Λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν, πᾶς ὃς ἂν ὁμολογήσῃ ἐν ἐμοὶ ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὁμολογήσει ἐν αὐτῷ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ θεοῦ·

verses.english: but whoever denies me before people will be denied before God.
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ ἀρνησάμενός με ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀπαρνηθήσεται ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.english: And everyone who speaks a word against the son of man will be forgiven; but whoever blasphemes against the holy spirit will not be forgiven.
verses.greek: καὶ πᾶς ὃς ἐρεῖ λόγον εἰς τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ τῷ δὲ εἰς τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα βλασφημήσαντι οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται.

verses.english: When they bring you before the synagogues and the rulers and the authorities, do not worry about how or what you are to answer, or what you are to say;
verses.greek: ὅταν δὲ εἰσφέρωσιν ὑμᾶς ἐπὶ τὰς συναγωγὰς καὶ τὰς ἀρχὰς καὶ τὰς ἐξουσίας, μὴ μεριμνήσητε πῶς ἢ τί ἀπολογήσησθε ἢ τί εἴπητε·

verses.english: for the holy spirit will teach you in that very hour what you ought to say."
verses.greek: τὸ γὰρ ἅγιον πνεῦμα διδάξει ὑμᾶς ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἃ δεῖ εἰπεῖν.

verses.english: Someone in the crowd said to him, "Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me."
verses.greek: Εἶπεν δέ τις ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, εἰπὲ τῷ ἀδελφῷ μου μερίσασθαι μετ’ ἐμοῦ τὴν κληρονομίαν.

verses.english: But he said to him, "Man, who appointed me a judge or arbitrator over you?"
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἄνθρωπε, τίς με κατέστησεν κριτὴν ἢ μεριστὴν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς;

verses.english: And he said to them, "Take care, and be on your guard against all greed; for one's life does not consist in the abundance of one's possessions."
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Ὁρᾶτε καὶ φυλάσσεσθε ἀπὸ πάσης πλεονεξίας, ὅτι οὐκ ἐν τῷ περισσεύειν τινὶ ἡ ζωὴ αὐτοῦ ἐστιν ἐκ τῶν ὑπαρχόντων αὐτῷ.

verses.english: And he told them a parable: "The land of a rich man produced plentifully.
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ παραβολὴν πρὸς αὐτοὺς λέγων· Ἀνθρώπου τινὸς πλουσίου εὐφόρησεν ἡ χώρα.

verses.english: And he thought to himself, 'What shall I do, for I have nowhere to store my crops?'
verses.greek: καὶ διελογίζετο ἐν ἑαυτῷ λέγων· Τί ποιήσω, ὅτι οὐκ ἔχω ποῦ συνάξω τοὺς καρπούς μου;

verses.english: Then he said, 'I will do this: I will pull down my barns and build larger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods.
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν· Τοῦτο ποιήσω· καθελῶ μου τὰς ἀποθήκας καὶ μείζονας οἰκοδομήσω, καὶ συνάξω ἐκεῖ πάντα τὸν σῖτον καὶ τὰ ἀγαθά μου,

verses.english: And I will say to my soul: Soul, you have ample goods laid up for many years; relax, eat, drink, be merry.'
verses.greek: καὶ ἐρῶ τῇ ψυχῇ μου· Ψυχή, ἔχεις πολλὰ ἀγαθὰ κείμενα εἰς ἔτη πολλά· ἀναπαύου, φάγε, πίε, εὐφραίνου.

verses.english: But God said to him, 'Fool! This night your soul is demanded of you; and the things you have prepared, whose will they be?'
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ θεός· Ἄφρων, ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ τὴν ψυχήν σου ἀπαιτοῦσιν ἀπὸ σοῦ· ἃ δὲ ἡτοίμασας, τίνι ἔσται;

verses.english: So it is with whoever stores up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God."
verses.greek: οὕτως ὁ θησαυρίζων ἑαυτῷ καὶ μὴ εἰς θεὸν πλουτῶν.

verses.english: And he said to his disciples, "Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, nor about your body, what you will wear.
verses.greek: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ· Διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν, μὴ μεριμνᾶτε τῇ ψυχῇ τί φάγητε, μηδὲ τῷ σώματι τί ἐνδύσησθε.

verses.english: For life is more than food, and the body more than clothing.
verses.greek: ἡ γὰρ ψυχὴ πλεῖόν ἐστιν τῆς τροφῆς καὶ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ ἐνδύματος.

verses.english: Consider the ravens: they neither sow nor reap, they have neither storehouse nor barn, and God feeds them. Of how much more value are you than the birds!
verses.greek: κατανοήσατε τοὺς κόρακας ὅτι οὐ σπείρουσιν οὐδὲ θερίζουσιν, οἷς οὐκ ἔστιν ταμεῖον οὐδὲ ἀποθήκη, καὶ ὁ θεὸς τρέφει αὐτούς· πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὑμεῖς διαφέρετε τῶν πετεινῶν.

verses.english: And which of you by worrying can add a single cubit to his span of life?
verses.greek: τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν μεριμνῶν δύναται ἐπὶ τὴν ἡλικίαν αὐτοῦ προσθεῖναι πῆχυν;

verses.english: If then you are not able to do so small a thing as that, why do you worry about the rest?
verses.greek: εἰ οὖν οὐδὲ ἐλάχιστον δύνασθε, τί περὶ τῶν λοιπῶν μεριμνᾶτε;

verses.english: Consider the lilies, how they neither spin nor weave; yet I tell you, even Solomon in all his glory was not clothed like one of these.
verses.greek: κατανοήσατε τὰ κρίνα πῶς οὔτε νήθει οὔτε ὑφαίνει· λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν, οὐδὲ Σολομὼν ἐν πάσῃ τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ περιεβάλετο ὡς ἓν τούτων.

verses.english: How much more you, you of little faith!
verses.greek: πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς, ὀλιγόπιστοι.

verses.english: And do not seek what you are to eat and what you are to drink, and do not be anxious.
verses.greek: καὶ ὑμεῖς μὴ ζητεῖτε τί φάγητε καὶ τί πίητε, καὶ μὴ μετεωρίζεσθε,

verses.english: For all the nations of the world seek these things, and your Father knows that you need them.
verses.greek: ταῦτα γὰρ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη τοῦ κόσμου ἐπιζητοῦσιν, ὑμῶν δὲ ὁ πατὴρ οἶδεν ὅτι χρῄζετε τούτων.

verses.english: Instead, seek the kingdom of God, and these things will be added to you.
verses.greek: πλὴν ζητεῖτε τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ ταῦτα προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν.

verses.english: Do not be afraid, little flock, for it has pleased the Father to give you the kingdom.
verses.greek: Μὴ φοβοῦ, τὸ μικρὸν ποίμνιον, ὅτι εὐδόκησεν ὁ πατὴρ δοῦναι ὑμῖν τὴν βασιλείαν.

verses.english: Let your loins be girded and your lamps burning,
verses.greek: Ἔστωσαν ὑμῶν αἱ ὀσφύες περιεζωσμέναι καὶ οἱ λύχνοι καιόμενοι,

verses.english: and be like people waiting for their master to come home from the wedding feast, so that they may open to him at once when he comes and knocks.
verses.greek: καὶ ὑμεῖς ὅμοιοι ἀνθρώποις προσδεχομένοις τὸν κύριον ἑαυτῶν πότε ἀναλύσῃ ἐκ τῶν γάμων, ἵνα ἐλθόντος καὶ κρούσαντος εὐθέως ἀνοίξωσιν αὐτῷ.

verses.english: Blessed are those servants whom the master finds awake when he comes; truly I tell you, he will gird himself and have them recline at table, and he will come and serve them.
verses.greek: μακάριοι οἱ δοῦλοι ἐκεῖνοι, οὓς ἐλθὼν ὁ κύριος εὑρήσει γρηγοροῦντας· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι περιζώσεται καὶ ἀνακλινεῖ αὐτοὺς καὶ παρελθὼν διακονήσει αὐτοῖς.

verses.english: If he comes in the evening watch and finds them so, blessed are they.
verses.greek: κἂν ἐν τῇ ἑσπερινῇ φυλακῇ ἔλθῃ καὶ εὕρῃ οὕτως, μακάριοί εἰσιν ἐκεῖνοι.

verses.english: But know this: if the master of the house had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have let his house be broken into.
verses.greek: Τοῦτο δὲ γινώσκετε ὅτι εἰ ᾔδει ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης ποίᾳ ὥρᾳ ὁ κλέπτης ἔρχεται, οὐκ ἂν ἀφῆκεν διορυχθῆναι τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: You also must be ready, for the son of man is coming at an hour you do not expect."
verses.greek: καὶ ὑμεῖς γίνεσθε ἕτοιμοι, ὅτι ᾗ ὥρᾳ οὐ δοκεῖτε ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἔρχεται.

verses.english: Peter said, "Lord, are you telling this parable for us or for all?"
verses.greek: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Πέτρος· Κύριε, πρὸς ἡμᾶς τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην λέγεις ἢ καὶ πρὸς πάντας;

verses.english: And the Lord said, "Who then is the faithful and wise steward, whom his master will set over his household, to give them their portion of food at the proper time?
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ κύριος· Τίς ἄρα ἐστὶν ὁ πιστὸς οἰκονόμος, ὁ φρόνιμος, ὃν καταστήσει ὁ κύριος ἐπὶ τῆς θεραπείας αὐτοῦ τοῦ διδόναι ἐν καιρῷ τὸ σιτομέτριον;

verses.english: Blessed is that servant whom his master will find so doing when he comes.
verses.greek: μακάριος ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος, ὃν ἐλθὼν ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ εὑρήσει ποιοῦντα οὕτως·

verses.english: Truly I tell you, he will set him over all his possessions.
verses.greek: ἀληθῶς λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ὑπάρχουσιν αὐτοῦ καταστήσει αὐτόν.

verses.english: But if that servant says in his heart, 'My master is delayed in coming', and begins to beat the menservants and the maidservants, and to eat and drink and get drunk,
verses.greek: ἐὰν δὲ εἴπῃ ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ· Χρονίζει ὁ κύριός μου ἔρχεσθαι, καὶ ἄρξηται τύπτειν τοὺς παῖδας καὶ τὰς παιδίσκας, ἐσθίειν τε καὶ πίνειν καὶ μεθύσκεσθαι,

verses.english: the master of that servant will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in pieces and put him with the unfaithful.
verses.greek: ἥξει ὁ κύριος τοῦ δούλου ἐκείνου ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ᾗ οὐ προσδοκᾷ καὶ ἐν ὥρᾳ ᾗ οὐ γινώσκει, καὶ διχοτομήσει αὐτὸν καὶ τὸ μέρος αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀπίστων θήσει.

verses.english: That servant who knew his master's will but did not get ready or act according to his will shall receive a severe beating.
verses.greek: ἐκεῖνος δὲ ὁ δοῦλος ὁ γνοὺς τὸ θέλημα τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ καὶ μὴ ἑτοιμάσας ἢ ποιήσας πρὸς τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ δαρήσεται πολλάς·

verses.english: But the one who did not know, and did what deserved a beating, shall receive a light beating. Everyone to whom much was given, of him much will be required; and from the one to whom much was entrusted, they will demand the more.
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ μὴ γνοὺς ποιήσας δὲ ἄξια πληγῶν δαρήσεται ὀλίγας. παντὶ δὲ ᾧ ἐδόθη πολύ, πολὺ ζητηθήσεται παρ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ᾧ παρέθεντο πολύ, περισσότερον αἰτήσουσιν αὐτόν.

verses.english: I came to cast fire on the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled!
verses.greek: Πῦρ ἦλθον βαλεῖν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν, καὶ τί θέλω εἰ ἤδη ἀνήφθη;

verses.english: I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how I am constrained until it is accomplished!
verses.greek: βάπτισμα δὲ ἔχω βαπτισθῆναι, καὶ πῶς συνέχομαι ἕως ὅτου τελεσθῇ.

verses.english: Do you think that I have come to give peace on earth? No, I tell you, but rather division.
verses.greek: δοκεῖτε ὅτι εἰρήνην παρεγενόμην δοῦναι ἐν τῇ γῇ; οὐχί, λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀλλ’ ἢ διαμερισμόν.

verses.english: For from now on in one house there will be five divided, three against two and two against three.
verses.greek: ἔσονται γὰρ ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν πέντε ἐν ἑνὶ οἴκῳ διαμεμερισμένοι, τρεῖς ἐπὶ δυσὶν καὶ δύο ἐπὶ τρισίν,

verses.english: Father will be divided against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law."
verses.greek: διαμερισθήσεται πατὴρ ἐπὶ υἱῷ καὶ υἱὸς ἐπὶ πατρί, μήτηρ ἐπὶ θυγατέρα καὶ θυγάτηρ ἐπὶ τὴν μητέρα, πενθερὰ ἐπὶ τὴν νύμφην αὐτῆς καὶ νύμφη ἐπὶ τὴν πενθεράν.

verses.english: He also said to the crowds, "When you see a cloud rising in the west, you say at once, 'A shower is coming', and so it happens.
verses.greek: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ τοῖς ὄχλοις· Ὅταν ἴδητε τὴν νεφέλην ἀνατέλλουσαν ἐπὶ δυσμῶν, εὐθέως λέγετε ὅτι Ὄμβρος ἔρχεται, καὶ γίνεται οὕτως·

verses.english: And when you see the south wind blowing, you say, 'There will be scorching heat', and it happens.
verses.greek: καὶ ὅταν νότον πνέοντα, λέγετε ὅτι Καύσων ἔσται, καὶ γίνεται.

verses.english: Hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of heaven and earth, but why do you not know how to interpret the present time?
verses.greek: ὑποκριταί, τὸ πρόσωπον τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ τῆς γῆς οἴδατε δοκιμάζειν, τὸν καιρὸν δὲ τοῦτον πῶς οὐκ οἴδατε δοκιμάζειν;

verses.english: And why do you not judge for yourselves what is right?
verses.greek: Τί δὲ καὶ ἀφ’ ἑαυτῶν οὐ κρίνετε τὸ δίκαιον;

verses.english: As you go with your accuser before a magistrate, make an effort on the way to settle with him, so that he does not drag you to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
verses.greek: ὡς γὰρ ὑπάγεις μετὰ τοῦ ἀντιδίκου σου ἐπ’ ἄρχοντα, ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ δὸς ἐργασίαν ἀπηλλάχθαι ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ, μήποτε κατασύρῃ σε πρὸς τὸν κριτήν, καὶ ὁ κριτὴς παραδώσει σε τῷ πράκτορι, καὶ ὁ πράκτωρ σε βαλεῖ εἰς φυλακήν.

verses.english: I tell you, you will not get out of there until you have paid the very last copper."
verses.greek: λέγω σοι, οὐ μὴ ἐξέλθῃς ἐκεῖθεν ἕως καὶ τὸ ἔσχατον λεπτὸν ἀποδῷς.

notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.28.1–8 follows the passage closely: the leaven of the Pharisees, nothing hidden that will not be known, "do not fear those who can only kill", "fear him who after killing has power to cast into Gehenna", which he says means the Creator, acknowledging and denying "before God", the sin against the holy spirit, and the spirit teaching in that hour. Epiphanius, sch. 29–30 quotes 12:4–5 in Greek ("to cast into Gehenna", βαλεῖν εἰς γέενναν) and states that the text had "before God" where canonical Luke has "before the angels of God". Both are printed. NA27 cites Marcion for the omission of "the angels of" in both 12:8 and 12:9.

Epiphanius, sch. 29: the text "did not have 'Are not five sparrows sold for two pennies? And not one of them is forgotten before God'". In his refutation he presses Marcion with it: "nothing happens without God, even if you take away what is about the sparrows". 12:7 ("the hairs of your head are all numbered… you are of more value than many sparrows") depends on 12:6, and Tertullian, who goes straight from 12:5 to 12:8, does not cite it, though it would have suited his argument for the Creator's care. It is classed "unattested, probably absent".

Tertullian, Marc. 4.28.9–11. He sets Jesus' refusal to divide the inheritance ("Who made me a judge over you?") against Moses, who was rejected with the same words when he tried to make peace between two Hebrews (Exod 2:14), and quotes God's words to the rich man: "Fool, this night they will demand your soul; and what you have prepared, whose will it be?" 12:15, 12:17–18 and 12:21 are not cited and are printed in grey.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.29.1–5 recasts the passage rhetorically, but the lilies "neither weave nor spin" (D: "neither spin nor weave"), not "toil nor spin" as in canonical Luke, and he quotes "Seek the kingdom of God". Epiphanius, sch. 31–34 states that the text lacked "God clothes the grass" (12:28a), quotes 12:30b and 12:31 ("the kingdom of God"), and states that 12:32 read "the Father", not "your Father". The text printed therefore goes from Solomon not clothed like the lilies to "How much more you, you of little faith!" 12:25–26 and 12:29 are not cited and are printed in grey. 12:33–34 ("sell your possessions") form a paragraph that no witness cites and are not printed.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.29.6–11 reads the girded loins and burning lamps as the life of faith, asks from whose wedding the master returns, and says that the thief is the devil, while the son of man comes as judge. He takes Peter's question to mean that the parable of the stewards is addressed to those "who would preside over the churches". Epiphanius, sch. 35 states that the master comes "in the evening watch", as in D and the Old Latin, not "in the second or third watch"; that reading is printed. Sch. 36 quotes 12:46. Tertullian reports that the Marcionites read "cut him in pieces" as mere separation (4.29.10); that is their reception, and the text has διχοτομήσει.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.29.12–16 quotes "I came to cast fire on the earth", "Do you think I came to bring peace on the earth? No, I tell you, but division", and the division of father and son, mother and daughter (Micah 7:6). He charges that "sword" is what is written and that Marcion changed it, but "sword" is Matthew's word (Matt 10:34); every Greek manuscript of Luke reads "division". He paraphrases 12:56 with "heaven and earth", the order of 𝔓45, 𝔓75 and D, which is printed. Epiphanius, sch. 37 quotes 12:58b. 12:50, 12:52 and 12:54–55 are not cited and are printed in grey.

Interpretation. In this text the Father knows what the disciples need, gives them the kingdom, and the holy spirit teaches them what to say. Tertullian's argument through 4.28–4.29 is that the God who provides food and clothing and judges is one and the same. The text as attested does not separate a providing God from a judging one. It speaks of the Father who gives and of the one to be feared who can cast into Gehenna (12:5), and Tertullian identifies them. Whether the community behind the text read the two as one cannot be decided from the witnesses.

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 11
chapters.preamble: Healing on the sabbath, and the kingdom compared. Jesus heals a woman bent over for eighteen years, "a daughter of Abraham whom Satan bound", and answers the leader of the synagogue with the ox or donkey watered on the sabbath. He compares the kingdom of God to a mustard seed sown in a garden and to leaven. Those who come to the door once the master has shut it will be told "I do not know where you come from", and will weep "when you see all the righteous in the kingdom of God, and yourselves held outside". In this text it is "the righteous", not Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and the prophets, whom they see in the kingdom. Two blocks of canonical Luke are not in this text, by Epiphanius' statement. The first is the Galileans killed by Pilate, the tower of Siloam and the barren fig tree (13:1–9). The second is the many coming from east and west, the warning about Herod and the lament over Jerusalem (13:29–35).

verses.english: Now he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath.
verses.greek: Ἦν δὲ διδάσκων ἐν μιᾷ τῶν συναγωγῶν ἐν τοῖς σάββασιν.

verses.english: And behold, there was a woman who had had a spirit of weakness for eighteen years; she was bent over and could not straighten herself at all.
verses.greek: καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ πνεῦμα ἔχουσα ἀσθενείας ἔτη δεκαοκτώ, καὶ ἦν συγκύπτουσα καὶ μὴ δυναμένη ἀνακύψαι εἰς τὸ παντελές.

verses.english: When Jesus saw her, he called her over and said to her, "Woman, you are freed from your weakness."
verses.greek: ἰδὼν δὲ αὐτὴν ὁ Ἰησοῦς προσεφώνησεν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Γύναι, ἀπολέλυσαι τῆς ἀσθενείας σου,

verses.english: And he laid his hands on her, and immediately she stood up straight and glorified God.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐπέθηκεν αὐτῇ τὰς χεῖρας· καὶ παραχρῆμα ἀνωρθώθη, καὶ ἐδόξαζεν τὸν θεόν.

verses.english: But the leader of the synagogue, indignant that Jesus had healed on the sabbath, said to the crowd, "There are six days on which work ought to be done; come on those days and be healed, and not on the sabbath day."
verses.greek: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ ἀρχισυνάγωγος, ἀγανακτῶν ὅτι τῷ σαββάτῳ ἐθεράπευσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς, ἔλεγεν τῷ ὄχλῳ ὅτι Ἓξ ἡμέραι εἰσὶν ἐν αἷς δεῖ ἐργάζεσθαι· ἐν αὐταῖς οὖν ἐρχόμενοι θεραπεύεσθε καὶ μὴ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ σαββάτου.

verses.english: The Lord answered him, "Hypocrites! Does not each of you on the sabbath untie his ox or his donkey from the manger and lead it away to water it?
verses.greek: ἀπεκρίθη δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος καὶ εἶπεν· Ὑποκριταί, ἕκαστος ὑμῶν τῷ σαββάτῳ οὐ λύει τὸν βοῦν αὐτοῦ ἢ τὸν ὄνον ἀπὸ τῆς φάτνης καὶ ἀπαγαγὼν ποτίζει;

verses.english: And this woman, a daughter of Abraham whom Satan bound for eighteen long years, ought she not to be set free from this bond on the sabbath day?"
verses.greek: ταύτην δὲ θυγατέρα Ἀβραὰμ οὖσαν, ἣν ἔδησεν ὁ Σατανᾶς ἰδοὺ δέκα καὶ ὀκτὼ ἔτη, οὐκ ἔδει λυθῆναι ἀπὸ τοῦ δεσμοῦ τούτου τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ σαββάτου;
